notes.ptu_payg_modeled_hypothesis: Modeled hypothesis, not measured PTU throughput.
notes.quality_guardrail: Read cost, throughput, and crossover views with the paired quality guardrail. Error bars are standard deviation where available, not confidence intervals.
notes.static_source: Rendered from same-origin static JSON; no live service calls are made.

chart_explainer.title: How to read this chart
chart_explainer.default_x_axis: Each position is one reasoning-effort cell for the benchmark: baseline, minimal, low, medium, high, or extra-high when present.
chart_explainer.default_y_axis: The vertical scale is the selected metric: {series}. Taller bars mean a larger value for that metric.
chart_explainer.default_bars: Each bar is the aggregate value for one effort cell. Compare bars left to right to see how the metric changes as effort rises.
chart_explainer.default_table: The table repeats the exact values behind the bars and includes sample counts plus standard deviation where available.

default.x_axis: Each position is one reasoning-effort cell for the benchmark.
default.bars: Each bar is one aggregate cell. Taller bars mean a larger value.
default.table: Use the table for exact values, standard deviation, and sample count.

cost_per_request.x_axis: Reasoning effort levels, from the baseline or lowest effort on the left toward higher effort on the right.
cost_per_request.y_axis: Mean USD per request. Taller bars mean the workload costs more per completed request under the PAYG lens.
cost_per_request.bars: Each bar summarizes the average bill for one effort cell. Read it beside the paired quality chart before deciding whether the spend is useful.
cost_per_request.table: The table gives the exact mean cost, standard deviation, and sample count used to draw the bars.

latency.x_axis: Reasoning effort levels for the same benchmark slice.
latency.y_axis: Mean latency in milliseconds. Taller bars mean users wait longer for the response.
latency.bars: Each bar is the average latency for one effort cell. Rising bars without quality gain indicate a slower but not better setting.
latency.table: The table gives exact latency, standard deviation, and sample count.

quality.x_axis: Reasoning effort levels for the benchmark slice.
quality.y_axis: Mean judge score. Taller bars mean the evaluator scored that effort cell higher.
quality.bars: Each bar is an aggregate quality score. Use it as the guardrail for cost and latency charts.
quality.table: The table gives the exact mean score, score spread, judge count, and sample count.

throughput_gain.x_axis: Reasoning effort levels for the benchmark slice.
throughput_gain.y_axis: Token-shape throughput factor. Lower bars mean fewer requests fit into the same token-shaped capacity.
throughput_gain.bars: Each bar compares the token shape of that effort cell with the baseline shape. Read this as planning evidence, not direct PTU measurement.
throughput_gain.table: The table gives the exact factor and token-per-request values behind the planning view.

token_composition.x_axis: Reasoning effort levels for the benchmark slice.
token_composition.y_axis: Mean token count per request for the selected token component.
token_composition.bars: The rendered bar uses the primary reasoning-token series so the hidden internal budget is visible. The table contains cached input, non-cached input, output, and reasoning tokens.
token_composition.table: Use the table to see the full token breakdown; the answer text alone does not expose reasoning tokens.

ptu_payg_crossover.x_axis: Reasoning effort cells used in the modeled crossover calculation.
ptu_payg_crossover.y_axis: Modeled break-even requests per minute. Taller bars mean PAYG must sustain a higher request rate before the PTU model crosses over.
ptu_payg_crossover.bars: Each bar is a modeled planning threshold, not measured PTU throughput.
ptu_payg_crossover.table: The table gives the modeled RPM, PTU hourly rate, minimum PTU floor, and related inputs.
